answer: Escrowed audience challenge. New identities must first answer a randomly drawn, time-boxed task from a live onyx pool whose answers are only verifiable by sustained work, and each attempt posts a refundable deposit released solely on a passing chain. A failed attempt forfeits the deposit to the pool and leaves a gale of fresh tasks, so cloning N times costs N deposits with expected recovery below one. Honest operators amortize one deposit, while a sybil farm faces a strictly negative echo of every marginal clone.
